2. The Petitioner filed Miscellaneous Cases No. 22-26 of 1984 under section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 before the Local Thana Magistrate, the Respondent 4, for redemption of the disputed property on the ground that the transfer of the land was a complete usufructuary mortgage. The respondent 4 on contest allowed the same by his order dated 19.3.85. Against the order First Appeal No. 69 (XIII) of 1984-85 was filed before the Respondent 3, the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Mymensingh who by his order dated 25.3.86 set aside the order of the Respondent 4. Against the order of the Respondent-S the petitioners filed Second Appeals Nos. 58-62 of 1986 before the respondent 2 who allowed the appeals and set aside the order of the first appellate authority and confirmed the order of the Respondent 4 by his order dated 5.9.90. Against the order of Respondent 2 appeals were filed before the Land Appeal Board, the Respondent 1. After hearing the parties and on examining the records the Respondent 1 passed the impugned order. 

 4. The contentions of Mr. Md. Abu Bakr Siddique requires examination of the relevant provisions of law in this regard. A reference to section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 does not support his contention for use of the expression "either by way of an out and out sale with an agreement to reconvey "in section 95A. In my opinion, the contention of Mr. Siddique that no registered document of reconveyance is necessary cannot be accepted in that the document for reconveyance is to be executed in the same sitting at a time when the document for transfer of land by way of out and out sale is executed and registered as without registration of the deed of transfer of an immovable property above the prescribed consideration does not vest title in the purchaser and unless the transfer vest the title the question of reconveyance does not arise. That is why the expression with an agreement to reconveyance" is used in section 95A of the Act, otherwise the expression will have no meaning. On the facts of this case and on perusal of the impugned order it is found that the Member of the Land Appeal Board has come to a finding on examination of the records that the transfer was out and out sale and the instrument of reconveyance of the land sold was obtained subsequent to filing of the pre-emption case under section 96 of the Act by respondent No.5, a co-sharer of the holding transferred. The law inserted in the said Act by section 95A is a beneficial one. In order to obtain a benefit under a law the party who seeks to obtain the benefit must strictly satisfy the authority that he has complied with the requirement of law in order to obtain the benefit. In this case the impugned order discloses otherwise. I find from the facts as stated in this petition and from the order impugned that there is serious question of disputed fact as to execution and date of execution of the instrument of reconveyance. It is well settled that Article 102 of the Constitution should not be invoked for deciding a serious disputed question of fact. Mr. Md. Abu Bakr Siddique relied upon an observation in the case of MA Hai and others vs. Trading Corporation of Bangladesh, 8 BLD 84 (AD) made by the Appellate Division that alternative remedy is no bar to Writ of certiorari. This is true, but which Mr. Siddique wants me to apply in this case has no relevancy to the facts of the present case. When the petitioners' cases fail on interpretation of section 95A and on disputed question of facts, it is not necessary to express opinion on alternative remedy for the purpose of deciding maintainability of this Writ petition.
